 LAS VEGAS (KSNV) — Heavy rain, flooding and even hail have hit parts of the Las Vegas valley on Friday.
 The National Weather Service issued a severe thunderstorm warning for the east Las Vegas valley until 1:45 p.m., citing public reports of hail and torrential rainfall.
 Heavy flooding was seen on Eastern Avenue north and south of Interstate 11/U.S. 95. The Weather Service says a flash flood warning remains in effect until 3:45 p.m.
 Three swift water rescues were reported at around 1 p.m. in Henderson:
 Lake Mead Pkwy and N. Pueblo Blvd: Crews responded to a person in a wash. Upon rescue, the person went into cardiac arrest and crews provided immediate care. The person was transported to a local hospital and was pronounced deceased.
 Lake Mead Pkwy east of the Lake Las Vegas entrance: Crews removed two people from a vehicle swept off the roadway by floodwaters. No injuries reported.
 N. Milan St near Drake St: Crews responded to a vehicle that became disabled attempting to cross floodwaters. One person was able to climb to the top of the vehicle, where crews made a rescue. No injuries were reported.
 News 3 has reached out to other local jurisdictions for information on swift water rescues and flooding.
 View post on X 
 Harry Reid International Airport has instituted a ground stop because of lightning through at least 3 p.m.
 NV Energy is reporting over 4,000 customers without power as of 1:40 p.m. The majority of those affected are in the central valley. That number was down to just over 2,000 customers by about 2:15 p.m.
